Command: Remove the ashes from the altar daily
Summary: The command: Remove the ashes from the altar daily (Leviticus 6:10). The priest, in linen garments, took up the ashes of the burnt offering and carried them to a clean place outside the camp.
Commandment: Remove the ashes from the altar daily, as prescribed in Leviticus 6:10.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: Each day the priest, in linen garments, took up the ashes and carried them to a clean place outside the camp — a ceremonial law of holy housekeeping. Its goal was to keep the altar clear and fit for the next day's offerings, the old fire's remains dealt with in order. It did not address a particular evil; its work was order and cleanliness in worship, not restraint. The ashes were not left to pile up; even the remains of holy fire were handled with care.
